newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, lifted by tight hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
The light supply was expected to offset reductions in slaughter for the third consecutive week as packers attempt to mend unprofitable operating margins, they said.

Hog slaughter on Tuesday was estimated by USDA at 313,000 head, which brought the week-to-date figure to 601,000, USDA reported. The weekly figure was down 3.4 percent from a week ago and down 10.3 percent from a year ago.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts on Monday were 88,000 head, 7,000 below the estimate, USDA said. Estimates for Tuesday at 90,000 head also could run lighter than the USDA estimate, several livestock dealers said.

Marketings were curtailed by a seasonal drop in hog supplies and active fieldwork by farmers. Farmers were trying to get as much planting done as they can before rain moves into the central Midwest overnight on Tuesday, sources said.
However, higher cash prices on Wednesday and rain could entice a few more farmers to bring hogs to market, some sources said.
